<button onclick="showMessage()">Click me</button>
<script>
function showMessage() {
  alert("Button clicked!");
}
</script>
Clicking the button calls showMessage(), which displays an alert.

<!DOCTYPE html>
<html>
<head><title>Changing Background Color</title></head>
<body>
  <button onclick="changeColor()">Change Background Color</button>
  <script>
    function changeColor() {
      document.body.style.backgroundColor = "lightblue";
    }
  </script>
</body>
</html>
JavaScript can be included in an HTML file by writing it inside a <script> element. It can also be placed in an external .js file and linked with a tag such as <script src="script.js"></script>.

<!DOCTYPE html>
<html>
<head><title>Change Background Color</title></head>
<body>
  <button onclick="changeColor()">Change color</button>
  <script>
    function changeColor() {
      document.body.style.backgroundColor = "lightblue";
    }
  </script>
</body>
</html>
When the button is clicked, its onclick handler calls changeColor(). The function changes the page's background color to lightblue.
